what: Load the Primary Biliary Cirrhosis (pbc) dataset from the survival package
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
text: Mayo Clinic trial primary biliary cirrhosis (PBC) liver conducted 1974 1984, n=424n=424 patients. 312 cases RCT, plus additional 112 RCT. Primary outcome (censored) time death

what: Create a Surv object using variables “time” and “status”, add this to the pbc dataframe
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
text: “1” patients received transplants, thus removed risk death, least due liver cirrhosis. Transplantation may thus related risk, qualify uninformative censoring. actually considered “competing hazard” high-risk patients may prioritized liver transplant - topic don’t get course. Instead, simply treat 0 (end study) 1 censored, 2 (death) event.
code: library(dplyr) ##  ## Attaching package: 'dplyr' ## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': ##  ##     filter, lag ## The following objects are masked from 'package:base': ##  ##     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union pbc2 <- pbc %>%   mutate(cens = status > 1.5) %>%   mutate(y = Surv(time, cens))

what: Plot a KM curve for all participants using library(survminer) function ggsurvplot().
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
code: library(survminer) ## Loading required package: ggplot2 ## Loading required package: ggpubr ##  ## Attaching package: 'survminer' ## The following object is masked from 'package:survival': ##  ##     myeloma fit <- survfit(y ~ 1, data = pbc2) ggsurvplot(fit)

what: Stratify by treatment and add a p-value to this plot (see ?ggsurvplot).
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
code: fit2 <- survfit(y ~ trt, data = pbc2) ggsurvplot(fit2, pval = TRUE)

what: Check whether these p-values correspond to results from a log-rank test.
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
code: survdiff(y ~ trt, data = pbc2) ## Call: ## survdiff(formula = y ~ trt, data = pbc2) ##  ## n=312, 106 observations deleted due to missingness. ##  ##         N Observed Expected (O-E)^2/E (O-E)^2/V ## trt=1 158       65     63.2    0.0502     0.102 ## trt=2 154       60     61.8    0.0513     0.102 ##  ##  Chisq= 0.1  on 1 degrees of freedom, p= 0.7

what: Perform a Cox proportional hazards regression, using the “trt” variable as a predictor.
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
code: fitcox <- coxph(y ~ trt, data = pbc2) summary(fitcox) ## Call: ## coxph(formula = y ~ trt, data = pbc2) ##  ##   n= 312, number of events= 125  ##    (106 observations deleted due to missingness) ##  ##         coef exp(coef) se(coef)      z Pr(>|z|) ## trt -0.05722   0.94438  0.17916 -0.319    0.749 ##  ##     exp(coef) exp(-coef) lower .95 upper .95 ## trt    0.9444      1.059    0.6647     1.342 ##  ## Concordance= 0.499  (se = 0.025 ) ## Likelihood ratio test= 0.1  on 1 df,   p=0.7 ## Wald test            = 0.1  on 1 df,   p=0.7 ## Score (logrank) test = 0.1  on 1 df,   p=0.7

what: Create a log-minus-log plot to test the proportional hazards assumption.
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
text: Using simpler method survminer:
code: library(survminer) ggsurvplot(fit2, fun = "cloglog")

what: Plot Schoenfeld residuals and perform Schoenfeld test for the above Cox model
title: Session 8 lab exercise: What it's about
code: fitzph <- cox.zph(fitcox) plot(fitzph) fitzph ##        chisq df    p ## trt    0.612  1 0.43 ## GLOBAL 0.612  1 0.43

title: Session 8: Survival analysis part 3
text: Just define stage ordered factor tests trend done automatically: Highly significant tests overall fit LRT, Wald, logrank test.
code: pbc.os <-   mutate(pbc.os, stageordered = factor(stage, ordered = TRUE)) fit <- coxph(Surv(time, os) ~ stageordered, data = pbc.os) summary(fit) ## Call: ## coxph(formula = Surv(time, os) ~ stageordered, data = pbc.os) ##  ##   n= 312, number of events= 125  ##  ##                   coef exp(coef) se(coef)      z Pr(>|z|)    ## stageordered.L  2.1759    8.8099   0.6801  3.199  0.00138 ** ## stageordered.Q -0.3469    0.7069   0.5248 -0.661  0.50867    ## stageordered.C  0.3209    1.3784   0.2990  1.073  0.28316    ## --- ## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ##  ##                exp(coef) exp(-coef) lower .95 upper .95 ## stageordered.L    8.8099     0.1135    2.3231    33.410 ## stageordered.Q    0.7069     1.4146    0.2527     1.977 ## stageordered.C    1.3784     0.7255    0.7671     2.477 ##  ## Concordance= 0.702  (se = 0.022 ) ## Likelihood ratio test= 52.74  on 3 df,   p=2e-11 ## Wald test            = 43.92  on 3 df,   p=2e-09 ## Score (logrank) test = 53.85  on 3 df,   p=1e-11
